lines.say: 2013: a storm dumped 2.98 inches of rain on La Porte over Halloween night, and gave Fort Wayne its wettest Halloween on record. 2014: a gust of 67 miles an hour off the lake at Michigan City. 2019: 2.2 inches of snow in Valparaiso. 2023: 1.4 inches of snow in South Bend, the second-snowiest ever.

lines.say: So why did it survive? Because it kept changing. A winter fire became a church feast. A church feast became a night for finding out who you'd marry. That became a night for breaking gates, and that became a deal: treat us, and we'll leave your gate alone.

lines.say: And every generation told itself the night was ancient, because that made it feel like it belonged to them. Maybe that's the real tradition. Not the turnip, or the pumpkin, or the candy. The story.

lines.say: Tell us yours. What did Halloween look like in La Porte when you were a kid? Which street gave out full-size candy bars? Put it in the comments. We read every one, and the best ones go in the next film.
